skill.name: w-onboard
skill.description: Guide a new developer from a cloned repository through setup, environment selection, local application startup, API verification, and the publishing handoff.
skill.summary: Move a developer from repository clone to a verified local application.
skill.author: blockmatic

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline-code references to documented commands and application routes. No semantic security findings were identified in the available evidence, and no evidence indicates that the skill performs unsafe external command execution.

static_findings.snippet: 1. Run the documented root setup script (Basilic: `pnpm setup`).
2. Decide local-only vs remote from the development-environments page named in `AGENTS.md`.
3. Start the documented web and API dev command (Basilic: `pnpm dev`).
5. Verify the app loads and reaches the API. Point at `/w-pr` when they are ready to publish work.
6. Docs: `/w-docs` if behavior or commands changed.

finding_verdicts.reason: The finding is triggered by the Markdown inline-code reference to pnpm setup, not executable Ruby or shell syntax. The line documents a repository setup command for the user or agent to run.
The backticks mark the AGENTS.md path as inline code in documentation. This line does not execute an external command or construct one from user-controlled input.
The finding matches the Markdown inline-code reference to pnpm dev. It is a documented development command, not Ruby backtick execution embedded in a program.
The backticks identify the /w-pr route in prose and do not invoke a shell. The line describes an application workflow rather than unsafe command execution.
The backticks identify the /w-docs route in documentation and do not represent executable Ruby or shell syntax. No external command execution is present in the cited text.

content.user_title: Onboard Developers to a Running Local App
content.value_statement: New developers often need a reliable path from a cloned repository to a working application. This skill turns project documentation into a focused setup, environment, verification, and handoff workflow.
actual_capabilities: Guide a developer through the documented root setup command.
Help choose between local-only and remote development environments using AGENTS.md guidance.
Start the documented web and API development workflow.
Verify that the application loads and reaches its API.
Direct a ready contributor to the /w-pr publishing workflow.
Identify when updated behavior or commands should be documented through /w-docs.
limitations: It depends on current repository documentation and the availability of the documented package manager.
It does not replace project-specific credentials, service access, or environment configuration.
It cannot guarantee that an application works when dependencies, services, or documentation are incomplete.
It does not independently design a new development environment outside the documented workflow.

use_cases.title: First-Day Developer Setup
use_cases.description: Guide a new contributor from a cloned repository through setup, environment selection, application startup, and API verification.

use_cases.title: Team Onboarding Handoff
use_cases.description: Give an engineering lead a consistent checklist for moving incoming developers from local setup to their first publishable change.

use_cases.title: Repository Workflow Review
use_cases.description: Check whether setup, development, verification, publishing, and documentation steps are clearly represented in the repository workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Start My Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: I cloned this repository. Guide me through the documented steps to reach a running local application, and identify anything I must provide.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Environment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the repository guidance to help me decide between a local-only and remote development environment. List the checks I should complete before choosing.

prompt_templates.title: Verify the Application
prompt_templates.prompt: Walk me through starting the web and API development workflow, then give me a concise checklist to verify that the application reaches its API.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare the Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my onboarding progress and tell me whether I am ready to publish work. Include the correct publishing route and note whether documentation updates are needed.

output_examples.input: I am new to this repository and want to get the application running.
output_examples.output: Run the documented root setup, choose the appropriate development environment from the repository guidance, start the web and API workflow, and confirm that the application reaches the API.

output_examples.input: The application is running and my change is ready.
output_examples.output: Verify the application once more, use the documented work-publishing route, and update the documentation route when behavior or commands changed.

best_practices: Follow the repository documentation before adding local workarounds.
Verify both the visible application and its API before publishing work.
Record changed commands and behavior in the project documentation.
anti_patterns: Do not skip setup or API verification because the web interface appears to load.
Do not choose a remote environment without checking the repository guidance.
Do not publish undocumented command or behavior changes.

faq.question: Who is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for developers, engineering leads, and maintainers who need a consistent repository onboarding workflow.

faq.question: What does the setup workflow cover?
faq.answer: It covers root setup, environment choice, development startup, application verification, and the publishing handoff.

faq.question: Does it configure credentials for me?
faq.answer: No. You must provide project-specific credentials, permissions, and services required by the repository.

faq.question: Can it choose between local and remote development?
faq.answer: It can help you use the repository guidance to make that choice, but the environment requirements remain project-specific.

faq.question: How do I know the application is ready?
faq.answer: The application should load and reach its API through the documented development workflow before you publish work.

faq.question: When should I update documentation?
faq.answer: Update the project documentation when your change modifies behavior or development commands.
